title: The Midnight Salt
premise: Juniper Brightwater has spent twelve years as the invisible keeper of the Saltgate, recording the Guild of Impossible Things' trades in souls, shadows, and second chances while hiding his own gift: he can hear what objects remember. When the crown's witch-hunters burn the guildhouse and seize the ledger, Juniper learns that his sister Wren sold her soul to the court beneath the mountain to buy his safety years ago—and the debt comes due at midwinter. To save her, Juniper must infiltrate the subterranean court, outwit its soul-broker queen, and choose between erasing his gift forever or claiming an inheritance of gatekeeping magic that will make him visible to every hunter in the realm. He claims it, reopens the Saltgate, and trades his own name into the ledger to buy Wren's soul back—ending the book with her free, him remembered by no one but her, and a new keeper's hand already reaching for the pen.
about_author: Tamsin Oyelaran is a former archivist who grew up in a coastal town famous for its salt marshes and its stubborn refusal to be mapped. She writes fantasy about people who keep records of things that were never supposed to happen.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A quiet night at the Saltgate: he balances the guild's ledgers, cataloguing impossible trades while listening to a doorknob remember its maker. Establishes his gift, his invisibility, and his careful loneliness. Emotional beat: contentment built on concealment.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Won't Say
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He finds a page torn from the oldest ledger, its edges burned, humming with grief. His mentor Odell deflects questions. First hint that Juniper's own history is written somewhere he can't read. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, in the city of Corrow. Criers announce the crown's hunt for the gifted; a neighbor is taken in daylight. Wren burns letters and prepares to flee toward Juniper. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Salt on the Threshold
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Odell teaches him the gate's closing rite 'just in case,' refusing to explain. The doorknob remembers fire. Juniper senses the guildhouse's wards thinning. Beat: dread arriving ahead of its cause.

chapters.title: Ashes Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Witch-hunters storm the guildhouse. Odell dies holding the door; Juniper escapes through the Saltgate with one ledger and Odell's iron key. Beat: guilt—the gate opened for him alone.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Fleeing across the marshes, he discovers roads literally forget him when he suppresses his gift—a survival trick with a cost. He resolves to reach Wren. Beat: isolation deepening.

chapters.title: A Sister's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reaches their childhood cottage and finds evidence someone searched it years ago—for Juniper. Flashback seeds: she once went away for a winter and came back 'lighter.' Beat: buried sacrifice stirring.

chapters.title: The Market of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He seeks the guild's black-market remnant in Corrow's undercity, trading a memory of Odell for passage. Learns the phrase 'the debt at midwinter.' Beat: first taste of how much he doesn't know.

chapters.title: Reunion, Unevenly
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Juniper and Wren reunite, but she flinches from his gift and lies badly about the winter she disappeared. He hears her locket remembering a signature in silver ink. Beat: love strained by secrets.

chapters.title: The Locket's Testimony
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Alone, he presses the locket for its memories: Wren signing a contract with the court beneath the mountain—her soul, priced against his safety. Beat: devastation; the hunt for him was always about her trade.

chapters.title: Terms of the Contract
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Confronted, Wren confesses: she sold her soul to Queen Vess of the Undercourt to hide Juniper from the old purge. At midwinter the debt collects. Beat: shame met, not forgiven yet.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Inn
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Witch-hunters track them; a fight in a snowbound inn forces them to use their gifts openly. They escape but are now marked. Beat: invisibility officially over.

chapters.title: The Descent Road
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. An exiled guild smuggler, Brannoc, agrees to guide them to the mountain's back door—for a price to be named later. Beat: wary alliance; foreshadowing the final trade.

chapters.title: The Village That Sold Its Shadows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Passing a village where everyone sold their shadows to survive famine, they see the cost of bargains unpaid. Wren nearly turns back. Beat: the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: The Back Door of the World
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They find the sealed stair beneath the mountain; Juniper's gatekeeper blood answers the lock where keys fail. Brannoc watches too closely. Beat: inheritance awakening.

chapters.title: First Door Below
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Inside, doors remember everyone who passed. Juniper reads the trail of a previous Brightwater who came down generations ago—and never came up. Beat: legacy as haunting.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They enter the Undercourt: a cathedral of contracts lit by bottled souls. Beauty and horror entwined. Beat: awe curdling into anger.

chapters.title: Audience with the Broker Queen
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Queen Vess receives them courteously, produces Wren's contract, and offers terms: a soul of equal weight by midwinter, or Wren stays forever. Beat: the trap of fair dealing.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Soul
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren secretly explores what 'equal weight' means, interviewing the court's indentured dead. She begins drafting a plan to substitute herself cleanly rather than let Juniper pay. Beat: sacrificial resolve.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Price
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Brannoc reveals his price: Juniper's gatekeeping gift, which Brannoc intends to sell to the hunters above. Betrayal, then a counter-offer Juniper can't refuse yet. Beat: trust inverted.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Undercourt
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In Vess's archive, Juniper finds the guild's founding ledger—and the torn page matching the one from chapter two, naming the first Brightwater gatekeeper and the original bargain that built the Saltgate. Beat: the inheritance revealed.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Opened
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Deciphering the page: the Brightwaters didn't just keep the gate—they made it, trading the family's collective memory to seal something worse than the court below. Beat: horror of ancestry.

chapters.title: Midwinter Eve Above
chapters.summary: Interlude, hunters' POV. Captain Ilsa Vane, leading the witch-hunt, receives orders not to kill Juniper but to bring him to the crown—who wants the gate. Beat: the hunt has a hidden client.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Midnight
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper offers Vess the founding ledger's secret instead of a soul. She counters: open the sealed inner gate for her, and Wren walks free. Beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Inner Gate
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They see the inner gate: behind it, the thing the first Brightwater traded everything to contain. Juniper understands why keeping it shut matters more than any soul. Beat: moral floor located.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper refuses Vess. She declares the contract executes at dawn; Brannoc sells their location to Vane's hunters anyway. Beat: all doors closing at once.

chapters.title: Siege in the Deep
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Hunters descend; three-way battle in the contract cathedral. Wren is captured by Vane; Juniper grabs the founding ledger and flees toward the inner gate. Beat: chaos as crucible.

chapters.title: The Bargain No One Asked For
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In custody, Wren offers Vane her soul freely if Juniper goes untouched—an echo of her original trade. Vane, unsettled, hesitates. Beat: sacrifice repeated, this time witnessed.

chapters.title: Reading the First Hand
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper fully opens himself to the founding ledger, absorbing the first Brightwater's memories: how to close a gate permanently, and what it costs—the keeper's name, erased from every record and mind. Beat: understanding the true price.

chapters.title: Dawn Clause
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the moment of collection, Juniper interrupts the ritual: he invokes an ancient clause—he may substitute 'a name of equal weight' for a soul. Vess, bound by her own law, must consider it. Beat: desperate legalism as heroism.

chapters.title: Vess's Counter-Read
chapters.summary: Queen Vess's POV. Vess probes the clause, tempted by a gatekeeper's name more than any common soul—but she wants the inner gate opened too. Standoff of interpretations. Beat: villain given depth.

chapters.title: The Trade at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Climax part one: Juniper agrees to open the inner gate a crack—not to release what's inside, but to show Vess why no one should hold it. What looks out through the crack terrifies even her. Beat: the monster behind the economy.

chapters.title: Closing Arguments
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Climax part two: Juniper performs the closing rite with Wren's help, sealing the inner gate permanently—which requires his name as payment. Vess, shaken, honors the clause: Wren's soul released. Beat: triumph purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren watches Juniper fade from every record, every memory—including hers, almost. Only the locket, holding his signature-memory, keeps one thread of him anchored. Beat: grief and wonder intertwined.

chapters.title: Above Ground, Unnamed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the mountainside, Juniper exists but is unrememberable; hunters walk past him. He keeps the locket like a lantern. Beat: freedom that feels like drowning.

chapters.title: The One Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, soul restored, hunts for the brother she can't quite recall, guided by the locket and her own stubbornness. She finds him. Beat: love as the exception to erasure.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Ledger
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Siblings begin anew: Wren becomes the public face, Juniper the unnamed hand, restarting the guild as something gentler—recording debts so fewer souls get sold. Beat: purpose reborn from ruin.

chapters.title: Vane's Report
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vane's POV. Vane files a report omitting Juniper entirely—her small rebellion—then resigns her commission, haunted by what she saw through the crack. Beat: even the hunter is changed.

chapters.title: The New Keeper's Hand
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Years later, a gifted child arrives at their door, fleeing hunters. Juniper begins teaching her the gate rites, knowing someday she'll inherit the cost too. Beat: inheritance as both burden and hope.

chapters.title: Signed in Silver Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, closing. Wren writes Juniper's name into a new ledger—the only place it exists—while he listens to the doorknob remember its maker. The gate holds; the debt is paid; the story ends where it began, warmer. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
